public_rationale: The historical assertion that inference costs had not gone down is contradicted. Before the post, Epoch reported declining benchmark evaluation costs after accounting for tokens consumed. This is more than a fall in advertised token prices. It does not establish that every application became cheaper or that spending on newer, harder frontier workloads was falling in August 2025; that part remains unestablished.
limitations: The contradiction applies to the categorical historical no-decline assertion.
Fixed benchmark capability is not the same measure as total application spending or continuously upgrading to frontier models.
Benchmark usefulness and possible overfitting limit generalization.
The page links datasets updated after the post; this assessment uses the dated article's stated findings, not those later downloadable datasets.
